Cautiously constructive tone: the Committee highlights strong labor markets and robust household spending, but flags weak business fixed investment and exports alongside inflation running below 2 percent—consistent with literature that investment is sensitive to financing conditions and internal funds (Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein, 1994) and that low, anchored inflation expectations dampen price dynamics in New Keynesian frameworks (Galí and Gertler, 1999; Woodford, 2003). The rate cut to 1.5–1.75% and ample-reserves operations target the interest-rate/liquidity channels documented to affect real activity (Sims; Romer and Romer), while acknowledging global headwinds in an open-economy setting (Obstfeld–Rogoff). Net sentiment is slightly positive but risk-aware.
